slides.title: Why does your dog *tilt* their head?
slides.sub: Three ideas from the AKC. Swipe.

slides.title: To hear you better.
slides.body: A tilt may move the ears. That could help your dog find where a sound comes from.

slides.title: To see your face.
slides.body: A dog's muzzle can block the view. A tilt may help them see your face and read it.

slides.title: Because it works.
slides.body: It often comes right before a treat or a walk. So your dog may do it again.

slides.title: Tell us about yours.
slides.body: Home boarding in Miramar. Serving Pembroke Pines and Broward.

posts.caption:
Why does your dog tilt their head?

The AKC says there is no one answer. Here are three ideas.

1. It may help them find where a sound comes from.
2. It may help them see your face past their muzzle.
3. It often comes before a treat or a walk, so they may keep doing it.

Every dog has little habits like this. Tell us about yours.
